references.text: Moses asks that the Lord should go with the people, the same plea for God's presence among them
Moses asks that the Lord should go with them, emphasizing the importance of God's presence
The Lord describes Israel as a stiff-necked people (עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹרֶף), the same expression Moses uses here
Israel is called a stiff-necked people, the same characteristic that Moses acknowledges in his prayer
Israel is described as a stiff-necked people, repeating this characterization
Moses reminds God of His servants and asks for forgiveness for the people's sin and disobedience
Moses asks for forgiveness for the people's sin (וְסָלַחְתָּ), the same plea for God's grace
A prayer for forgiveness for sin and wrongdoing for the Lord's name's sake
Israel as God's inheritance and treasured possession (וּנְחַלְתָּנוּ), God takes them as His own portion
The Lord's people are His inheritance, the same theme of Israel as God's possession
Moses has found favor in the Lord's sight (מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ), the same expression for favor
Warning against hardening the heart like a stiff-necked people, referring to Israel's disobedience
Direct continuation of the same dialogue where Moses asks for God's presence and forgiveness for the people.
Theological parallel: Humanity's plea for forgiveness for sin meets God's promise to heal apostasy.
